newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB still generous, remains alert to any changes.
newsitem.headline: SNB still generous, remains alert to any changes.

text.p: Swiss National Bank board member Bruno Gehrig said the central bank was maintaining its generous monetary policy and that it remained alert to changes.
Gehrig, in the text of a speech, said the SNB had to ensure price stability could be maintained longer-term but added "inflationary fears at this time are hardly justified."
"Against this background we will continue our generous monetary policy and thus consolidate the monetary requisites for an economic recovery," Gehrig said.
"But we will remain watchful and critical, in order to take the curve -- no matter which way -- correctly and in time," he said.
He said that the central bank was keeping to a middle path with respect to its policy.
"We believe the path we are presently on is a middle way between the two evils of 'too much' and 'too little'," he said.
He said that any contribution to growth by the SNB must also take long-term stability into account.
He said bank lending meanwhile remained sluggish, and it was hard to say how long the braking effect would continue on the economy.

"In the end, one can assume that our economy, in view of substantial not utilised capacities, can stand an expansion in production without a quick rise in price levels," Gehrig said, adding that investments in capital equipment in the otherwise sluggish 1990s had developed very positively.
